title: KV bank grooming and transient slot levelling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We observe persistent small-slot fragmentation in the KV cache under realistic continuous-batching workloads. Short sequences and variable token spans create many sub-page holes that increase GPU memory pressure and trigger expensive background compactions. This ticket designs and implements a banked allocation + transient slot levelling strategy to reduce fragmentation, improve live defrag efficiency, and keep latency within SLOs during aggressive batching.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight bank layer on top of the current slab allocator: allocate KV entries from sized banks (tiny/short/long) chosen by predicted token span. Implement transient slot levelling: when a request frees a slot, the slot becomes a transient bucket for a short TTL and receives preferential migration candidates so adjacent holes can be coalesced opportunistically. Add a low-priority GPU background reshuffle that runs during idle cycles to compact banks with high fragmentation ratios. Use probabilistic slot migration during long-generation tails to avoid adding latency to hot requests. Expose fragmentation metrics and automatic thresholds that trigger reclamation passes.
decisions: 1) Use three banks by default (SHORT <=128 tokens, MEDIUM 129-512, LONG >512) with configurable boundaries. 2) Make transient slot TTL adaptive based on kernel idle fraction (shorter TTL when GPU busy). 3) Background reshuffle runs at lowest GPU priority and pauses if p99 latency exceeds configured SLO margin. 4) Hot-key soft-pinning: entries with >X hits/sec are parked in stable slots to avoid churn. 5) Initial rollout gated behind a runtime flag and an observability dashboard.
implementation_notes:
- Add bank index metadata (8-bit) to KV descriptor to avoid large allocation metadata cost.
- Allocation path: estimate token span at request start via prompt length + expected continuation; choose bank, attempt first-fit within bank; if failure, borrow from adjacent bank with exponential backoff.
- Transient bucket: freed slots are pushed to per-GPU transient ring with expiry timestamp; migration worker takes candidate slots and performs memcpy style relocation to create contiguous segments.
- Background reshuffle: mark source and target slot ranges and run locality-preserving coalescence using CUDA kernels that perform batched memcpy and metadata updates.
- Ensure strict ordering of KV indexes during migration: use per-request token-epoch counters to ensure readers skip in-flight moves.
- Implement gates in serving runtime: migration must not block fast-path token generation; perform moves only between attention steps or on CPU-pinned copies when necessary.
- Introduce fragmentation_ratio = 1 - (largest_contiguous_free / total_free) as primary metric and microburst_fragmentation (short-term variance) for alarming.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Synthetic benchmark: under mixed load (60% short, 30% medium, 10% long sequences) fragmentation_ratio reduces by >=60% at steady state versus current allocator.
2) 95th/99th token latency does not regress by more than 5% under identical batching config.
3) Peak GPU memory usage reduces by >=10% for typical workload traces recorded from customers A/B.
4) No increase in tail error rate or KV corruption incidents during a 48 hour canary.
5) Metrics surfaced on Console: fragmentation_ratio, transient_bucket_hits, bank_utilization, reshuffle_throughput.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for bank selection, TTL expiry, and borrowing path.
- Microbench harness that replays production traces and measures fragmentation_ratio and mem usage.
- End-to-end perf job against staging cluster with realistic batching from workload traces.
- Fault-injection tests: kill reshuffle worker mid-copy, simulate OOM during migration, ensure safe rollback.
- Canary rollout to 2 dedicated pods, monitor p99 latency, memory, and error rates for 48h before wider rollout.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: Feature behind runtime flag, internal triage cluster only. Phase 1: Canary on 2 pods for 48h with aggressive telemetry. Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 20% traffic across dedicated pool with monitoring-based automatic rollback. Phase 3: Full rollout once metrics stable for 7 days. Include kill-switch to disable background reshuffle alone if needed.
Gate: automatic pause of reshuffle if p99 token latency increase >5% for 10 minutes.
